verse1.philosophical_explanation: Bhagavad Gita Chapter 10 Verse 1 offers a layered teaching on disciplined action, inner clarity, and God-centered wisdom, presenting dharma as a harmonizing principle that integrates duty, knowledge, devotion, and self-mastery. In Vedantic reflection, the outer event is never merely external; it mirrors the inner field of the seeker where attachment, fear, pride, compassion, and discernment contend for dominance. The text therefore asks the reader to cultivate viveka, sustained discrimination between the permanent and the impermanent, while remaining active in righteous responsibilities. It also emphasizes that true strength is not aggression but alignment with satya, ahimsa in intent, self-restraint, and surrender to the Divine will. Ethical life in Sanatana Dharma emerges through disciplined action offered without egoic possessiveness, where one performs svadharma with humility and accountability. This teaching is socially relevant because it links personal transformation with collective order: families, communities, and governance remain stable only when conduct is rooted in justice, gratitude, and reverence for truth. Spiritually, the section invites bhakti and contemplative awareness, showing that liberation-oriented living can begin within ordinary duties when the heart is purified through right understanding and service.
verse1.scripture_text: श्रीभगवानुवाच | भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः | यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ||१०-१||

verse.sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच | भूय एव महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः | यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ||१०-१||
verse.translation: 10.1 The Blessed Lord said Again, O mighty-armed Arjuna, listen to my supreme word which I will declare to thee who who art beloved, for thy welfare.
verse.transliteration: śrībhagavānuvāca . bhūya eva mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ . yatte.ahaṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā ||10-1||
